chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Old Ship AME and Mount Zion Baptist: choir practice and the blues in the church
summary: His mother played at Old Ship Church and grandmother at Mount Zion, so he attended both choirs; he links blues to gospel expression.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: You said that your mother played in one church and your grandmother in another.
What were the churches? Do you remember any of the churches?

Well, one was Old Ship Church. That was an AME Church, African Methodist Episcopal, and my grandmother played in Mount Zion. That was a Baptist church. So that meant that I had to go to choir practice at both churches. The young men's Christian endeavor, and the BYPU, and oh, boy, and that fire and brimstone really got me. But --

-- Union, I imagine, yes. And the Methodist was a Young Men's Christian Endeavor. Yes, so it was the same thing, just different name. But any way, that was the south at that time. That's what most of the black musicians -- that's the way they performed. You know, this was their outlet, yes. So you got -- your blues came from there, because I hear some of these gospel churches now, I'm sure you hear them on the air, and it's all blues, you know. But this is their way of expressing themselves.
